APAR STATUS

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  a LOAD PARTITION PARALLELISM utility job failed with ABENDC03
   and MSGDSNU1036I when the INDDN data set for the INTO TABLE PART
   x statement was a DUMMY data set and the template for DISCARDDN
   doesn't have SPACE keyword.
   
   DSNU1036I   174 10:08:17.38 DSNURELD - UNABLE TO ESTIMATE SPACE
   REQUIREMENTS FOR DISCARDDN
   DSNU012I    174 10:08:19.07 DSNUGBAC - UTILITY EXECUTION
   TERMINATED, HIGHEST RETURN CODE=8
   
   DB2PARALL/K
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All DB2 9 for z/OS utility users of LOAD     *
   *                 with partition parallelism.                  *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: ABENDC03 after a LOAD with partition    *
   *                      parallelism ended with RC8 and message  *
   *                      MSGDSNU1036I - UNABLE TO ESTIMATE SPACE *
   *                      REQUIREMENTS FOR DISCARDDN.  Some of    *
   *                      the SYSREC data sets were defined as DD *
   *                      DUMMY and the DISCARD data sets were    *
   *                      dynamically allocated using TEMPLATES   *
   *                      without SPACE parameters.               *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION: Apply corrective PTF when available          *
   ****************************************************************
   A LOAD with multiple INTO TABLE PART x INDDN SYSRECnn
   DISCARDDN DISCn statements where some of the SYSREC data sets
   were defined as DD Dummy, and TEMPLATES were used for the
   DISCARD data sets with no SPACE attributes, ended with RC8.
   MSGDSNU1036I - UNABLE TO ESTIMATE SPACE REQUIREMENTS FOR
   DISCARDDN was issued.  An ABENDSC03 followed.
   
   During LOAD PARTITION PARALLELISM processing, a DD DUMMY SYSREC
   data set caused a flag to get set which indicated that no space
   estimate was available from the sysrec data set for the discard
   data set.  This led to MSGDSNU1036I and the RC8.  However,
   LOAD should tolerate the SYSREC DD DUMMY when allocating the
   DISCARD data sets.
   
   The ABENDC03 was issued because this error condition left
   some of the data sets opened.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  LOAD PARTITION PARALLELISM code has been modified to tolerate
   SYSREC DD DUMMY data sets.

title: IBM How to export and import keys from an HSM-enabled IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance - United States
text:
Title: IBM How to export and import keys from an HSM-enabled IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How do I export and import private keys between the same or different Hardware Security Module (HSM) enabled IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance? 

ANSWER
HSM-enabled DataPower appliances support the export of private keys using the crypto-export command. For key export to work, various conditions must be met: 

 * HSMs must be initialized and in the same key sharing domain on exporting and importing machines 
 * The private key in question must be marked exportable at keygen time (see keygen's exportable option) 
 * HSMs on exporting and importing machines must share internal key-wrapping keys (see hsm-clone-kwk command). A key-wrapping key is a key that encrypts another key.


Each HSM has a special key inside of it, the key-wrapping key, that is used to encrypt exported private keys (and to decrypt imported private keys). If the goal is to restore exported keys to the same appliance, then you don't need to worry about hsm-clone-kwk, red keys, or the hsm-domain parameter. That is because the key-wrapping key at import time will already match the key-wrapping key at export time (since the HSM device is the same). If the goal is to move exported keys from one appliance to another one, then all of the steps in this section must be followed :- 

First, the two HSMs in question must be both be initialized and in the same key sharing domain. This means that they must both be initialized in the same mode (both in Security Level 2 or both in Security Level 3). In Security Level 2 mode, they must have used the same hsm-domain parameter during hsm-reinit (this parameter has a default value that is the same on all appliances). In Security Level 3 mode, they must have used the same red PED key during hsm-reinit (and the second initialization must not have overwritten the key value from the first initialization). 

Second, the key to be exported must be exportable. The exportability of keys is immutable. It is determined at keygen time, and it is controlled by that command's exportable parameter. If a key was created outside of the appliance (not using keygen), then it is always considered exportable. 

Finally, before the crypto-export crypto-import sequence, the key-wrapping keys must be synchronized using the hsm-clone-kwk command. This command must be run four times: once on the source HSM appliance (with the key-wrapping key you are copying), once on the destination HSM appliance, once again on the source HSM appliance, and once again on the destination HSM appliance. Each time the command is run, it will need the output file from the previous step (as the input to the current step) which must be moved manually (usually with the copy command). 

Once all of this has been done, then private keys may move from system to system with crypto-export and crypto-import. 

Note that the non-HSM appliance can export keys immediately at keygen time, but never at a later time. 

For additional information refer to the online Info Center [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wsdatap/v3r8m2/index.jsp?topic=%2Fxi50%2Fwelcome.htm] and search for "PIN entry device".

Note: You will need to sign into the documentation portal with your IBM Registration ID and password.

title: IBM Error -9 with Client Access - United States
text:
TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Error

Error number -9
DMS-E-GENERAL, A general exception has occurred during operation
'asynchronous open'
[IBM][CLIENT ACCESS/400 ODBC V2 Driver][DB2/400 SQL] Internal Driver Error.

or 

Error number -5
DMS-F-BUGCHECK, An internal system failure has occurred during operation 'fetch'
DMS-E-ODBC_INTERNAL, An internal error (ODBC error -9) has occurred within the ODBC gateway
[Microsoft][ODBC DLL] Function Sequence Error

when attempting to submit a query in Impromptu via Client Access ODBC. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
This error is being returned from the Client Access ODBC driver. Try the following and contact Client Access if the problem persists

Confirm that a successful connection can be made outside of Impromptu.
Run an ODBC trace to trap the full error message. 
Confirm that the Client Access being used is not the Client Access for DOS. 

Change the following line in the ODBC.ini, in the section for Client Access. Restart Impromptu for this to take effect. 

[AS400CAWIN]
Driver=c:\cawin\ehnodbc3.dll
Description=Client Access/400 ODBC driver

ODBCRemarks=0 ; *0=OS/400 object description, 1=SQL/400 object comment -> change 0 to 1 in this line

Installing the latest Client Access ODBC driver may also resolve this problem.

title: IBM running DB2 Text Search routines may receive CIE00340 error - United States
text:
TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When you run DB2 Text Search routines to create, update, or drop indexes, you may receive CIE00340 error as below example: 


$ db2 "CALL SYSPROC.SYSTS_CREATE('MYSCHEMA', 'MYTEXTINDEX','PRODUCT (NAME)', '', 'en_US', ?)"

SQL20427N An error occurred during a text search administration procedure or

command. The error message is "CIE00340 Cannot start executable program

"cieadmsv". ". SQLSTATE=38H14

However, at the same time, if you use DB2 Text Search commands to create, update or drop indexes, it can run successfully.

For example:


$ db2ts "CREATE INDEX MYSCHEMA.MYTEXTINDEX FOR TEXT ON PRODUCT(NAME) CONNECT TO SAMPLE"

CIE00001 Operation completed successfully.

NOTE: The issue won't occur in DB2 V10.1 or later due to different design of Text Search routines.


CAUSE
DB2 Text Search routines are fenced DB2 routines created at the DB2 database server side when you enable a database for Text Search Extender support. Therefore they need to be run inside a db2fmp process belonging to the db2 fenced user. However, by default the db2 fenced user is not granted the execute permission to the Text Search server executables that will be called by the db2 fenced routines, therefore running Text Search Routines will throw above error. 

On the other hand, because DB2 Text Search commands are run under the db2 instance user, by default they have been granted Execute permission to these Text Search server executables, so they should run fine.


DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
When the routines report the error, the corresponding db2diag.log shows: 


2014-05-18-12.46.54.483848+600 I129913A485 LEVEL: Error
PID : 7995456 TID : 1 PROC : db2fmp (10153) 0
INSTANCE: db2inst9 NODE : 000 DB : SAMPLE
APPID : *LOCAL.db2inst9.140422040349
EDUID : 1 EDUNAME: db2fmp (10153) 0
FUNCTION: DB2 UDB, Text Search, CieProcess::startProcess, probe:200
MESSAGE : CIE reason

title: IBM PK01725: ABEND0C4 IN DFSOCM30 DURING IMS SHUTDOWN - United States
text:
SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  ABEND0C4 in DFSOCM30 caused by the timing of events driven
   during shutdown.  A /CHE FREEZE command causes an SCI
   deregistration (dereg) call.  Before the SCI dereg, a /DBR
   command comes in and an AWE is sent to IMS from SCI.  The
   dereg process cleans up storage which is being used by the
   /DBR command.  Therefore, we hit an ABEND0C4.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: IMS/ESA rel 910 users who use SCI and OM.    *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: ABEND0C4 in DFSOCM30 during IMS         *
   *                      shutdown.                               *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION: INSTALL CORRECTIVE SERVICE FOR APAR/PTF      *
   ****************************************************************
   A /CHE FREEZE command was entered and shortly thereafter a /DBR
   command came in through the SPOC.  The processing of the /DBR
   command was passed into the control region and had already
   acquired some CSA storage when suddenly that storage was freed
   causing the abend when access to it was made.
   
   The storage was freed because the /CHE FREEZE shutdown process
   had reached the point in which it makes a degregister calls to
   SCI, OM and RM.  These calls resulted in the CSA storage being
   freed.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  AIDS: RIDS/SYS RIDS/CNTRL SYS CNTRL
     DEP: NONE
     GEN:
   
   *** END IMS KEYWORDS ***
   An orderly synchronization of shutdown has been established in
   the control region when commands can be entered from the SPOC
   via OM and SCI.  This synchronization provides a counter of
   active OM commands in the system, and logic in the shutdown
   process to only issue the SCI, OM and RM deregistration calls
   when the counter has reached zero.  In addition a fence is
   established to prevent further commands.
   
   The following parts have been changed:
   
   DFSSXIN0 - this is the SCI Input Exit for IMS. It receives
              control when an IMSplex member issues a request to
              be processed by IMS.  If it is an OM request and
              neither the shutdown-fence flag nor the shutdown-
              needs-posting flag is on, it increments the active
              OM command counter before proceeding with the
              request.  If either flag is on, it immediately
              returns with a return code of of IRC_ENVIRON
              and a reason code of IRSN_SHUTDOWN to OM if
              IMS is shutting down when the command is received.
   
   DFSOCM00 - this is the router module for OM-originated IMS
              commands.  When it receives a request from DFSSXIN0
              and the SCDPTRM0 flag is on, the command is ignored,
              the counter is decremented, and if the counter has
              gone to zero, shutdown is posted.  This module then
              waits for next request.
              If the flag is not on, the command is passed to the
              command action module.  Upon return the counter is
              decremented and if it has gone to zero and the
              SCDPTRM0 flag is on, this module IPOSTs shutdown
              and waits for next request.
   
   DFSOCM10 - this is the router module for OM-originated IMSplex
              commands.  When it receives a request from DFSSXIN0
              and the SCDPTRM0 flag is on, the command is ignored,
              the counter is decremented, and if the counter has
              gone to zero, shutdown is posted.  This module then
              waits for next request.
              If the flag is not on, the command is passed to the
              command action module.  Upon return the counter is
              decremented and if it has gone to zero and the
              SCDPTRM0 flag is on, this module IPOSTs shutdown
              and waits for next request.
   
   
   DFSTERM0 - this is the control task termination module.  It
              has been changed to only issue the deregistration
              calls if the count is zero and after it has set
              on the fence bit to prevent further commands.  If
              the count is not zero when it reaches this point,
              it sets the bit to request POSTing and then IWAITs.
              When posted it sets the fence bit and proceeds
              with shutdown.
   
   ISCD     - adds a new field, DFSOMCCT, to contain the count of
              active OM commands.  In the hi-order byte of this
              field, a flag byte is defined which contains two
              flag-bits: SCDDREGD, which indicates that dereg
              calls have been made, and SCDPTRM0, which indicates
              that shutdown needs to be posted when the count
              reaches zero.

   Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2004 12:20:57 GMT

   Server: IBM HTTP Server/V5R3M0
   Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2004 12:20:58 GMT
   .
   As can be seen, this header contains multiple HTTP/1.1, Server,
   and Date header lines which is not according to RFC 2616.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of the WebSphere HTTP Server for   *
   *                 OS/390 and z/OS that write non-nph           *
   *                 (No Parse Headers) CGIs that use the         *
   *                 cgiutils module to set headers.              *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Customer uses the cgiutils module in a  *
   *                      CGI and gets duplicate headers.         *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   The customer is using the cgiutils module in a non-nph CGI.
   The cgiutils module creates a full set of response headers for
   a nph (No Parse Headers) CGI.  A nph CGI response is passed
   through the HTTP Server with no action by the HTTP Server on
   either the response headers or content body.
   When used with a non-nph CGI both the cgiutils module and the
   HTTP Server create headers, thereby causing some duplicate
   headers.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Changed the code in the cgiutils module to recognize when it is
   called in a non-nph (No Parse Headers) CGI so that ONLY the
   headers requested are created.
   -
   Prior to this APAR if -status was set by the cgiutils module
   the following response headers were generated automatically:
       HTTP/1.1 200 OK
       MIME-Version: 1.0
       Server: IBM HTTP Server/V5R3M0
       Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2004 21:06:17 GMT
   After application of this APAR these headers will ONLY BE
   generated automatically if the CGI to be executed is prefixed
   with "nph-".
   
   The following COMPID is affected by these changes:
   
   5697D4300 HTTP Server for OS/390 and z/OS  Version 5
   
   PTF04C
   The code changes are stored in CMVC under defect PQ84618.
   
   ==============================================================
   PQ84618 is changing documentation
   --------------------------------------------------------------
   HTTP Server Planning, Installing and Using
   Part 7. Appendixes
   Appendix A. Commands
   Cgiutils Command
   --------------------------------------------------------------
   Please replace:
   Note: If you want to supply your own no-parse header (nph)
   programs specifically to return your own return values, the
   name of the program must begin with nph-.  This prevents the
   server header from overriding your return value with the
   standard server return value.
   -
   with the following:
   Note: If you want to supply your own no-parse header (nph)
   programs specifically to return your own return values, the
   name of the program must begin with nph-.  This causes the
   HTTP Server to act as a pass-through mechanism from the nph
   CGI to the browser.  The HTTP Server will create no headers
   and will not translate the response body from EBCDIC to ASCII.
    -
   A nph CGI must create both response headers and response body
   in the correct network codepage.  Such as ISO8859-1 ASCII
   English.
   -
   If you use the cgiutils command inside a non-nph CGI to create
   response headers; the HTTP Server will treat the headers and
   any response content normally, and they will be translated
   to the proper codepage as specified by the "DefaultNetCP"
   configuration directive.

title: IBM Guardium v10 drill down report has no results - United States
text:
TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When right clicking and selecting a drill down report in v10 Guardium, the drill down report unexpectedly has no results.
When viewing the drill down report directly, not via drill down path, it has results. 

CAUSE
The number of columns displayed in the GUI for the report must match the total number of columns possible for that report, otherwise drill down from it will not work. 

At the time of writing this is true in Guardium v10 up to GPU p200. There is a plan to allow drill down to work no matter how many columns are displayed. Please check the release notes in more recent GPUs to check if this change is included.


DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
1. Check the number of columns displayed on the report where you are doing drill down from. This can be done from the 'Column Configuration' screen. For example in the Aggregation/Archive Log: 

[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21996447&aid=1] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21996447&aid=1]

If not all columns are selected, drill down from this report will not work.

2. To check the exact underlying error, run support must_gather app_issues [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21971158] (or 'User Interface' option from GUI must gather page). While the debugger is running, try and open the drilldown report.

In the resulting mustgather file, inside <date>-debug.log file an error like the below will appear:

==============Mon Nov 21 14:00:39 CET 2016===================
Thread: http-bio-8443-exec-8 - java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 6, Size: 6
at java.util.ArrayList.rangeCheck(ArrayList.java:647)

title: IBM S or U table locks used in online index reorg with ALLOW WRITE ACCESS. - United States
text:
TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 During online index reorg with ALLOW WRITE ACCESS, sometime you would see S or U table locks are acquired on table. 

CAUSE
An online index reorganization operation with ALLOW WRITE ACCESS provides good concurrency and flexibility to both user and DBA. 
Throughout the life cycle, it can hold multiple types of locks. Besides the locks mentioned in IBM Knowledge Center, sometimes you will see S or U locks are acquired on the table.

You can use db2pd command to monitor the index reorganization operation.

db2pd -db <db_name> -locks -applications -reorgs index

There are three phases for an online index reorganization, Scan, Build and Catchup.

In the following example, S table lock is captured by db2pd command during Catchup phase.

title: IBM Executing the db2rbind command recieves the SQL0440N error - United States
text:
TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 When execuing the db2rbind command, the following SQL0440N error is returned:

Package 'NULLID.STADMH03' of database 'DB1' did not succeed to
rebind. UniqueID = 41414141414D495A
sqlcode = -440; sqlerrmc = SNAPSHOT; sqlrrp = SQLNQ25ESNAPSHOT

SQL0440N No authorized routine named "SNAPSHOT_CNTRFS" of type
"FUNCTION" having compatible arguments was found.

How can SQL0440N be avoided when executing the db2rbind command? 

ANSWER
Please find the associated bind file name in the following list by searching the package name, "STADMH03":
DB2 v9.7 Bind File and Package Name List
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21516118 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21516118]
(In this example, st_admin.bnd is the associated bind file name for STADMH03)

Then please run below commands for removing the SQL0440N error.

db2 CONNECT TO <database_name>
db2 BIND $HOME/sqllib/bnd/<bind file name> BLOCKING ALL GRANT PUBLIC SQLERROR CONTINUE
(In this example, db2 BIND $HOME/sqllib/bnd/st_admin.bnd BLOCKING ALL GRANT PUBLIC SQLERROR CONTINUE )
db2 terminate

In case of such errors, the bind files should be explicitly bound. A topic regarding binding files can be found in the Information Center:

Binding bind files after installing fix packs
http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/db2luw/v9r7/topic/com.ibm.db2.luw.qb.server.doc/doc/t0024970.html [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/db2luw/v9r7/topic/com.ibm.db2.luw.qb.server.doc/doc/t0024970.html]

As part of a fix pack installation on the server, binding of the database utilities (IMPORT, EXPORT, REORG, the Command Line Processor) and the CLI bind files occurs automatically. However, if you install a fix pack on the client or an error occurs, you can manually bind the database utilities and the CLI bind files. Different subsets of bind files must be bound for the DB2 Database for Linux, UNIX, and Windows and host or System i® database servers.

title: IBM PQ88192: A POSSIBLE INTEGRITY EXPOSURE EXISTS WHEN USING FDBR IF IMS IS RESTARTED BY ARM OR AUTOMATION AND /ERE RUNS BEFORE FDBR ENDS. - United States
text:
SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  A possible data integrity exposure exists when using FDBR.
   If IMS is restarted by ARM or automation, it is possible that
   /ERE and FDBR Recovery process could run concurrently,
   resulting in damage to databases or the IMS log stream.
   No customer has seen this problem but it was verified
   internally.
   This apar will also remove the restriction that ARMRST=Y
   cannot be in effect for both the CTL region and the FDBR region.
   (Currently, specification of ARMRST=Y for FDBR disables
   ARM restart for the CTL region).
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All IMS R910 FDBR users.                     *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: A possible integrity exposure exists    *
   *                      when using FDBR if IMS is restarted by  *
   *                      arm or automation and /ERE runs before  *
   *                      FDBR ends.                              *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION: INSTALL CORRECTIVE SERVICE FOR APAR/PTF      *
   ****************************************************************
   A possible data integrity exposure exists when using FDBR.  If
   IMS is restarted by ARM (i.e. ARM=Y was specified for the IMS
   system while ARM=N was specified for the FDBR system) or user
   automation, it is possible that the /ERE of the restarted IMS
   and the FDBR recovery process could run concurrently, resulting
   in damage to databases and/or the IMS log stream.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  AIDS: RIDS/SYS RIDS/CNTRL SYS CNTRL
     DEP: NONE
     GEN:
   
   *** END IMS KEYWORDS ***
   Both the IMS and FDBR systems have been modified to issue a
   global resource serialization ENQ in order to prevent a failed
   IMS system from being restarted before FDBR completes its
   recovery.
   
   When FDBR senses that the IMS system has abended, its first
   action before it begins recovery is to issue an exclusive
   global-wide ENQ using a QNAME of IMSVSFDR and a RNAME of ten
   characters consisting of the subsystem ids of the IMS and FDBR
   systems along with the IMS version number.  FDBR holds this
   ENQ until it completes the recovery.
   
   Early in an IMS restart, the system makes a TEST ENQ call using
   the same QNAME and RNAME to determine whether the resource is
   available.  If it is not, then FDBR must be in recovery and IMS
   waits for 3 seconds before retrying the TEST ENQ.  When the
   resource becomes available, IMS proceeds with its restart.
   Note that the IMS system does not ever obtain nor hold the ENQ.
   
   Because the ENQ now prevents a restarted IMS system from
   interfering with the FDBR recovery, the restriction that
   ARMRST=Y cannot be in effect for both the IMS system and the
   FDBR region simultaneously is removed.  Previously, an ARMRST=Y
   specification for FDBR disabled the ARM restart for the IMS
   system.  With this maintenance ARMRST=Y can be specified for
   both system and each will be restarted by ARM if it abends
   independently of the other.
   
   The following parts have been changed:
   
   DFSFDR00 - issues the ENQ for the FDBR system.
   
   DFSFDR10 - now issues the FDBR ARM Ready call, instead of
              the ARM Associate call which negated the ARMRST=Y
              setting of the IMS system.
   
   DFSRST00 - issues the TEST ENQ with a wait of 3 seconds
              between calls if the resource is not available.
   
   DFSTERM0 - issues the FDBR DEQ for the resource after the
              locks have been released and the log closed.
   
   Additional Keywords: CMDERE CMD/ERE

title: IBM Changes in the default user identifier between WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 classes for JMS and WebSphere MQ V7.1 classes for JMS - United States
text:
Title: IBM Changes in the default user identifier between WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 classes for JMS and WebSphere MQ V7.1 classes for JMS - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 You have configured a WebSphere Application Server WebSphere MQ messaging provider connection factory without an Authentication Alias and do not programmatically supply user identifier information when creating a connection to a queue manager. You notice a change in the default behaviour between WebSphere Application Server versions regarding the user identifier flowed on the MQCONN to the target WebSphere MQ Queue Manager:

- When using WebSphere Application Server v7.0 and v8.0, no user identifier value (blank) is passed to the queue manager. 

- When using WebSphere Application Server V8.5, a non-blank user identifier value is passed to the queue manager. 

In the latter case, you receive the following exception when creating a connection to a queue manager:

JMSCMQ0001: WebSphere MQ call failed with compcode '2' ('MQCC_FAILED') reason '2035' ('MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED') 

Is this change in behaviour expected? 

ANSWER
WebSphere MQ access control is based on user identifiers. There is a deliberate change in the default behaviour between the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 classes for JMS and the WebSphere MQ V7.1 (and later) classes for JMS regarding the default user identifier flowed to the queue manager.
From the WebSphere MQ V7.1 classes for JMS onwards, a non-blank user identifier is always flowed to the queue manager when creating a connection to WebSphere MQ. This is true even if no user identifier has been specified, or a blank or null user identifier has been specified; for example by calling:

MQConnectionFactory.createConnection();

or:

MQConnectionFactory.createConnection(“”, “”);

or:

MQConnectionFactory.createConnection(null, null);

In the case where a null or blank user identifier has been specified, the WebSphere MQ V7.1 and later classes for JMS will query the value of the Java System Property user.name. The value of this property is flowed to the queue manager for authorization.

As a result, if the user identifier specified by the Java System Property user.name is not authorized to access the queue manager, the queue manager will return an exception to the WebSphere MQ classes for JMS with Reason Code MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED and the connection to the queue manager will not be established.

This change in behaviour could affect topologies that previously relied on the default behaviour in the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 classes for JMS that flowed a blank user identifier when establishing a CLIENT mode transport connection. The expectation that a blank or null user identifier will be flowed by default, and that the user identifier that started the WebSphere MQ server-connection channel would be used by the queue manager when performing the authorization checks, is no longer valid from the WebSphere MQ V7.1 classes for JMS.

In the case outlined above, system administrators that are currently relying on the default behaviour of the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 classes for JMS should review their configurations regarding the use of user identifiers and authorization. This might also help to improve security within their WebSphere MQ topology.


In summary, the change in behaviour will affect users of:

- The WebSphere MQ V7.1 and later classes for JMS.

- The WebSphere MQ V7.1 and later JCA Resource Adapter that includes the classes for JMS.

- Versions of WebSphere Application Server that include the WebSphere MQ V7.1 and later JCA Resource Adapter. Currently this is WebSphere Application Server V8.5.0.0 and later.


The com.ibm.mq.jms.ForceUserID Java System Property

A Java System Property called “com.ibm.mq.jms.ForceUserID” was introduced as part of APAR IZ49302 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IZ49302] and included from WebSphere MQ V6.0.2.8 and WebSphere MQ V7.0.1.

The changes made as part of this APAR could be used to change the default behaviour in the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 classes for JMS regarding the user identifier value flowed to the queue manager when creating a connection.

This property is no longer valid from WebSphere MQ V7.1. Setting this property will have no affect on the WebSphere MQ V7.1 classes for JMS and later.

Other Useful Resources

WebSphere MQ Documentation

The WebSphere MQ Documentation contains a section on planning user authorization which also includes a description on access control for clients. A link to this section in the WebSphere MQ V7.1 Documentation is as follows:

WebSphere MQ > Security > Planning for your security requirements >> Planning authorization [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/wmqv7/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.mq.doc/zs14070_.htm]

Technotes

A Technote is available that explains J2C Authentication Aliases and how they can be used to configure the user identifier flowed to a queue manager when creating a connection: 

Enterprise applications, the WebSphere Application Server WebSphere MQ messaging provider connection factories and Authentication Aliases explained [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21580097]

       All message is put to CLQ03 on FMQX.
   .
   The reason of QMGR FMQO is not select is that CLQMGR flag shows
   it is not Joined eventhough Cluster(FMQCLT03) has Joined falg.
   .
   verbx csqxdprd 'subsys=FMQO,clus=1' shows
    CLQMGR.
     Qm(FMQ0
     Flags(Local Repos CLUSRCVR-Def In-Use )
     Cluster(FMQCLT01                 )
      Flags(Local Repos CLUSRCVR-Def )
     Cluster(FMQCLT03                 )
      Flags(Local Repos CLUSRCVR-Def Joined )
     Cluster(FMQCLT02                 )
      Flags(Local Repos CLUSRCVR-Def )
   .
   The Joined ( rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER ) flag should be ON if
   there is a least one cluster with Joined flag.
   The problem is the loss of the rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER
   flag in the RFXCLUSTER_Q_MGR Flags field in the fastnet cache
   when the CLUSRCVR channel for the QMGR is DEFINE REPLACEd in
   CSQINP2.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX
 *  REFRESH CLUSTER or RESUME QMGR CLUSTER(FMQCLT03) will be bypass
   the problem until next restart of MQ.
   Or
   Remove DEFINE REPLACE CHANNEL of the CLUSRCVR
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of WebSphere MQ for z/OS Version 6 *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: After ALTER/DEFINE of a CLUSRCVR        *
   *                      channel using a CLUSNL when the first   *
   *                      cluster in the namelist has been        *
   *                      suspended, the MQQMF_AVAILABLE value in *
   *                      the MQWDR passed to a cluster workload  *
   *                      exit may be incorrectly set causing the *
   *                      exit to make incorrect decisions.       *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   When a CLUSRCVR channel is defined in more than one cluster
   using a CLUSNL if the FIRST cluster is suspended using SUSPEND
   QMGR CLUSTER(x) and while the CHINIT is down the CLUSRCVR
   channel is ALTERed (say to change the batch size - or even via a
   DEFINE REPLACE command in CSQINP2) then when the CHINIT is
   subsequently started during reconciliation processing in
   rrmRecoClqMgr the rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER flag in the
   RFXCLUSTER_Q_MGR Flags field is incorrectly set OFF.
   This flag is redefined as MQQMF_AVAILABLE in the MQWDR and
   therefore may cause a customer cluster workload exit to
   incorrectly route messages if it relies on this flag.
   A REFRESH CLUSTER command will correct the flag, but the effect
   lasts only until the next ALTER of the CLUSRCVR channel (or QMGR
   restart if a DEFINE REPLACE for the channel exists in CSQINP2).
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  In module CSQXRRMF:
   Routine rrmChangeClqMgr has been changed to correctly set the
   rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER flag in the requested ClusQMgr
   passed to rrmRecoClqMgr.
   Distributed Apars IZ14977 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IZ14977] and IZ36482 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IZ36482] have been ported to
   rrmRecoClqMgr.
   Routine rrmRecoClqMgr has been changed to correctly set the
   flag rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER in the ClqMgr entry if any of
   the Clus entries have the flag set.
   This ensures that the MQQMF_AVAILABLE value in the MQWDR will
   be correctly set for use by Cluster Workload Exits.

title: IBM Vulnerability Scanner shows a lot of vulnerabilities when scanning Lotus Protector. - United States
text:
vulnerability; CVE; LPMS TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
What causes a Vulnerability Scanner to show a large list of vulnerabilities when scanning Lotus Protector?

ANSWER
Often, the tests that Vulnerability Scanners are doing are not probing if the appropriate service is actually vulnerable, but they are just looking at the version number of the installed packages (e.g. 'rpm -q apache2' or trying to get the version information when connecting to the service) and then comparing it against a database. 
Such a "Vulnerabilty Scan" does not take into account:

- that there might be an older version that has a backport of the appropriate fix
- that some modules are not loaded at all / that some functionality of the modules is not enabled

For its SuSE Enterprise Linux Novell/SuSE does usually not quickly jump to newer base versions of the packages but will stay on the base version of a package and fixes the vulnerability in that version (= backporting of a fix). 

There are several methods to check if the installed package is vulnerable to
a certain CVE:

1. Using the Novell Support Websites

- the underlaying OS of Lotus Protector is SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 10
x86
- get the info which version is installed
rpm -q packagename (e.g. openssh, apache2)
- use 'Google' to search for <cve-number> + Novell

You will usually find a web-page at support.novell.com where you will find information in which package the issue is fixed thoroughly
example: CVE-2007-4752

Result: Installed version = openssh-4.2p1-18.38.3 / problem fixed with
version >= openssh >= 4.2p1-18.30

2. Using the changelogs that are part of the installed packages

rpm -q -changelog <package-name> | grep -i <cve-number>

example a: check if the installed openssh package is vulnerable against
'OpenSSH X11 Cookie Local Authentication Bypass Vulnerability -
CVE-2007-4752'

rpm -q -changelog openssh | grep -i CVE-2007-4752

- fixed checking of an untrusted cookie, CVE-2007-4752 [#308521]

example b: check if the installed apache2 package is vulnerable against
'Apache Server 2.x Prior To 2.2.14 Multiple Vulnerabilities - '

rpm -q -changelog apache2 | grep -i -E "(CVE-2009-3095|CVE-2009-3094)"

- fixed CVE-2009-3094 (The ap_proxy_ftp_handler function in
modules/proxy/proxy_ftp.c in the
- fixed CVE-2009-3095 (access restriction bypass in mod_proxy_ftp module)

example c: sometimes a vulnerability is fixed in the associated library -->
'Apache APR and APR-util Multiple Integer Overflow Vulnerabilities -
CVE-2009-2412'

rpm -q -changelog libapr-util1 | grep -i CVE-2009-2412

- fixed Overflow flaw in apr_pool and apr_rmm APIs (CVE-2009-2412,

3. Checking which apache modules are loaded:

apache2ctl -t -D DUMP_MODULES

Loaded Modules:

core_module (static)
mpm_prefork_module (static)
http_module (static)

Conclusion:
Doing vulnerability scans means to carefully go through the results and to try to find out which are valid findings and which are 'False Positives'. We do frequently do vulnerability scans with our product therefore it is very unlikely that there are old "CVE's" found which are NOT False Positives. If there are findings which seem to be real vulnerabilities of the product, please contact Technical Support.

ABSTRACT
This document provides information on the IBM DataPower Gateway Firmware Support Lifecycle.

CONTENT
IBM® DataPower® Gateway is a purpose-built gateway that provides security, traffic control, mediation and optimized access to a full range of mobile, web, application programming interface (API), service-oriented architecture (SOA), B2B and cloud workloads. It supports multi-cloud deployment and is available in Docker container, Linux application, VMware virtual machine and physical appliance form factors.

IBM provides flexible support options to meet the needs of your business and minimize any business impact. The IBM DataPower Gateways end-of-service support policy applies differently between hardware and firmware.

Hardware 

DataPower physical appliance hardware is supported for a minimum of five years, starting at the General Availability of the new product. Beginning with the 8436 models, standard appliance service and support is available for five years from the end-of-marketing (EOM) date as described in the IBM Appliance Support Handbook [http://www.ibm.com/support/customercare/sas/f/applhandbook/home.html].

For end-of-service information on physical appliances, see IBM DataPower Gateways End of Service dates [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21317845]. 

Firmware 

Businesses are building modernized digital platforms to drive innovation and disruption within the industry. IBM DataPower Gateways are a core component in these platforms and it needs to deliver new business functionality to keep pace with business innovation.

Effective with DataPower Gateway firmware V7.6 [https://www.ibm.com/common/ssi/cgi-bin/ssialias?infotype=AN&subtype=CA&htmlfid=897/ENUS217-265&appname=USN], DataPower introduces a Continuous Delivery (CD) model to accelerate delivery of new capabilities and meet market needs. DataPower CD will consist of two releases:

 1. CD release approximately once per quarter  * Only the most recent CD release is supported at a given time.
    
    
 2. Long Term Support (LTS) release every 12 months.  * LTS releases are for customer seeking enhanced stability and do not wish to upgrade on the CD schedule, while CD releases are intended for customers seeking the latest features.
     * The first LTS release post 7.6 GA will be within two years. Subsequent LTS releases will occur every 12 months.
     * LTS releases will be supported for a minimum of 2 years.
    
    

Firmware V7.6 and later have no extended support plan available for any release of DataPower Gateway. IBM will publish a notice of support discontinuance (end-of-service) for a LTS releases at least 12 months before the effective date.

Firmware V7.5 and earlier will remain on the traditional IBM DataPower Gateway support model where they will be supported for a minimum of 2 years. There is no extended support plan available for any of these releases. IBM will publish a notice of support discontinuance (end-of-service) for releases at least 12 months before the effective date.

Title: IBM How do I process Sparse data objects Identified in the Audit - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How do I turn on sparse data object processing 

ANSWER
After harvesting a volume, the audit may show "skipped - cannot 
access data object", with a sparse data object message recorded in the details section. 

To correct this problem, ensure that no jobs are running. SSH into the Data Server(s) and enter the following command at the prompt; 


psql -U dfuser dfdata -c "insert into adminknobs (name,value,description,valuetype,use) VALUES ('read_sparse_files','1','Read sprase data objects','int','1')"

It should return the following;

INSERT 0 1

if so, enter the following command and wait for the UI to come back up;

service siqinit restart

You can now run harvests as normal and sparse data objects will be processed. If your are using a policy which backs up the original files and just leaves a sparse file viewable that when accessed, will pull the original file forward, you may run into space issues. This is because SIQ will be accessing every sparse file, so the sparse files' size on disk will grow to the same size as the original file.

title: IBM Converting from IPAT - United States
text:
KnowledgeCollection TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Converting from IPAT 

ANSWER


 This document contains the procedures for converting from a traditional IPAT network to an IPAT with aliasing network, and for converting from IPAT with aliasing to a traditional network. This information applies to HACMP Enhanced Scalability 4.5 and higher and AIX 5.1 and higher. 




 CONVERTING FROM A TRADITIONAL IPAT NETWORK TO AN IPAT WITH ALIASING NETWORK (IPAT=IP ADDRESS TAKEOVER) 
 1. Stop the cluster on all nodes.  
    
    
 2.  Configure the existing service labels and boot interfaces for the network so that they use different subnets. This will require changes to both the HACMP and AIX configurations.  
    
    
 3.  On an HPS network, remove the old boot labels from the HA configuration and configure the base HPS adapter addresses as HACMP boot interfaces. For other network types, convert the existing standby interfaces into boot interfaces.  
    
    
 4.  Verify that the network is configured to support gratuitous ARP by checking the NIM settings for the network type.  
    
    
 5.  Ensure that the USE IP ALIASING FOR IPAT setting is not "disable". (smitty cm_config_nets_change_net.select or see options under Configure IP Based Networks SMIT screen)  
    
    
 6.  Synchronize the cluster topology. 




 CONVERTING FROM IPAT WITH ALIASING TO A TRADITIONAL NETWORK 
 1.  Stop the cluster on all nodes.  
    
    
 2.  If the network is using multiple boot interfaces on each node, convert all but one of them into standby interfaces, leaving just one boot interface per node on the network.  
    
    
 3.  Reconfigure the service labels so that they are on the same subnet as the remaining boot interfaces.  
    
    
 4.  Set the USE IP ALIASING FOR IPAT field to disable for the network.  
    
    
 5.  Synchronize the cluster topology.

text:
Title: IBM Using -Xgc:preferredHeapBase with -Xcompressedrefs - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 "Why does the JVM report a native out-of-memory (NOOM) when using compressed references? I am using a 64bit JVM and I clearly have plenty of memory left. How can I resolve this problem?" 

CAUSE
 

*In this note, please refer to Java Versioning: Java Version.Release.ServiceRelease.FixPack 
ex: Java 7.1.4.6 is the same as Java 7.1 SR4 FP6 is the same as Java 7 R1 SR4 FP6. 
The IBM JVM will automatically use compressed references [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/javasdk/v6r0/topic/com.ibm.java.doc.diagnostics.60/diag/understanding/mm_compressed_references.html]when using a maximum heap size less than 25GB. This automated behavior was introduced in Java 6.1.5.0 and Java 7.0.4.0*. Compressed references (CR) decreases the size of Java objects making better use of available memory space. This better use of space results in improved JVM performance. *(Java 7.0.1.1 and later uses compressed references by default on z/OS) 

See Introducing WebSphere Compressed Reference Technology [ftp://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/webserver/appserv/was/WAS_V7_64-bit_performance.pdf] for detailed information on how Compressed References work. 

"When using compressed references, the size of the field used in the Java object for the Class Pointer and the Monitor/Lock is 32 bits instead of the 64bits that would be available in non-compressed mode. Because we are using 32 bits to store the location of these, and they are located in native (non-Java heap) memory, they must be allocated in the first 4GB of the address space - the maximum range we can address with the 32 bits." ~IBM Java Development Team 

If the Java heap itself is small (-Xmx), the JVM may allocate it in the lower 4GB of address space along with the Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks. If these Class Pointers, Monitors/Locks and Java heap (if included) cannot fit in the lower 4GB, a native out of memory (NOOM) [http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/library/j-nativememory-linux/] will be thrown. 
ANSWER
Why Use Compressed References? 

Below the 4GB mark, the JVM does not have to perform any compression/decompression of the address pointer at runtime. Therefore, the best performance will be attained if the Class Pointers, Monitors/Locks and Java heap can all be contained comfortably within the lowest 4GB of the address space. 

 

Determining Address Location of Java Heap Memory 

To verify if the Java heap has memory regions below the 4GB mark, check the "Object Memory" section in the javacore:

Convert the "start" address from the hex value to a GB value [http://ss64.com/convert.html]. In the example below, 0x000000000F010000=0.23GB which is below the the 4GB (0x0000000100000000) mark.



 * [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21660890&aid=1]


Setting the Preferred Heap Base with -Xgc:preferredHeapBase 

Starting with Java 6.1.6.0 and Java 7.0.5.0, and later, the JVM will determine if the Java heap will fit comfortably in the lower 4GB. If it is too large, the JVM will automatically allocate the Java heap above the 4GB mark (APAR IV37797 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IV37797]). 



NOTE: In IBM System z platforms (i.e. z/OS and z/Linux), automatic shift of the heap above the 4GB address space does NOT occur because on these platforms, there is an additional performance penalty 
associated with higher shift values. To resolve Native OOM issues due to a shortage of heap memory in the lower region on z platforms, use -Xnocompressedrefs (see below). 
See related: IBM Knowledge Center - JVMJ9GC089W [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSYKE2_7.0.0/com.ibm.java.messages/diag/appendixes/messages/j9gc/message_jvmj9gc089.html] However, in earlier Java 6.1 and Java 7.0 versions (earlier than Java 6.1.6.0 and Java 7.0.5.0), if the Java heap can not fit in the lower 4GB, a NOOM will occur. To avoid this problem, the generic JVM argument [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21417365] -Xgc:preferredHeapBase=<address> [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/javasdk/v6r0/topic/com.ibm.java.doc.diagnostics.60/diag/understanding/mm_compressed_references.html] can be used to ensure the Java heap is allocated above the 4GB address space. This will leave more room for the Class Pointer and Monitor/Lock memory. 

 * 
 * 
 * 
 * 
 * 
 * 
 * This will locate the Java heap starting at the 4GB mark thus leaving the lower 4GB for the other processes.


Increase Maximum Heap Size to Force Heap Allocation Above the 4GB mark 

Another way to ensure that the heap is allocated above the 4GB mark (Java 6.1.6.0 and Java 7.0.5.0 and later) is to set a maximum heap size equal to or greater than 4GB. For example -Xmx4G will ensure that the heap will have to be allocated above the 4GB mark. This will not work in earlier versions of the JVM since these earlier versions allowed the heap to straddle the 4GB mark, placing part of the memory above and some below (fixed as part of APAR IV37797) . 

 

Further Investigation 

If after setting -Xgc:preferredHeapBase=<address> or -Xmx4G a NOOM is still encountered (Java 6.1.6.0 and Java 7.0.5.0 and later), then further investigation is required at the application level. Look to decrease the size and usage of the applications Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks. Additionally, there are some WebSphere Application Server troubleshooting methods that may help reduce the native memory footprint. See: IBM Troubleshooting native memory issues [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg21373312].

Reserving Low-Memory Space with -Xmcrs

If there is still free memory in the system when a Native OutOfMemory (NOOM) occurs, then the problem may be a shortage of memory in the low-memory region (under 4GB). Even if the Java heap is located above this boundary, other data associated with Java objects can be located in the low-memory region.

The OS memory allocator will deal out low-memory freely, thus memory resources in the lower boundary may run out. Later when the JVM tries to allocate memory for an artifact which is required to be allocated in low-memory (because the JVM has only reserved a 32bit pointer for it) it fails and throws an OutOfMemoryError.

Starting in Java 6.0.16.3, Java 6.1.8.3, Java 7.0.8.10, Java 7.1.2.10, there is a parameter -Xmcrs [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSYKE2_6.0.0/com.ibm.java.doc.diagnostics.60/diag/appendixes/cmdline/xmcrs.html] which allows the JVM to increase the amount of low memory it reserves on startup. With this setting, as long as the low-memory usage by the JVM does not exceed the -Xmcrs value, NOOM in the lower boundary will be avoided.

To set this parameter, first decide what a reasonable value for your lower memory requirements may be. Reasonable value is unique to each environment so there is not a general recommendation.


 * -Xmcrs<reasonable_value_for_lower_memory>

Disabling Compressed References with -Xnocompressedrefs As a last resort, if the native memory still can not be contained under the 4GB mark, you can set -Xnocompressedrefs [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/javasdk/v6r0/topic/com.ibm.java.doc.diagnostics.60/diag/appendixes/cmdline/Xnocompressedrefs.html] as a generic JVM argument. [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21417365] Using -Xnocompressedrefs will remove the use of compressed references and therefore remove the lower 4GB memory restriction on the Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks. This will however, result in a significant increase in Java heap memory requirements. It is not uncommon for 70% more heap space to be required. Due to the increased memory requirements it is strongly advised that the Java heap size is adjusted to a larger value and garbage collection is monitored and retuned as required.

Additionally, some benchmarks show a 10-20% relative throughput decrease when disabling compressed references: "Analysis shows that a 64-bit application without CR yields only 80-85% of 32-bit throughput but with CR yields 90-95%. Depending on application requirements, CR can improve performance up to 20% over standard 64-bit." See:ftp://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/webserver/appserv/was/WAS_V7_64-bit_performance.pdf [ftp://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/webserver/appserv/was/WAS_V7_64-bit_performance.pdf].

Before using -Xnocompressedrefs as a solution, first rule out the possibility of a native memory leak. Since using -Xnocompressedrefs will allow the the native memory to grow unbounded, a leak in native memory will lead to process size growth eventually leading to a process that needs to be paged out. The paging will incur performance overhead which will eventually lead to an unstable environment. Therefore careful consideration must be used when selecting -Xnocompressedrefs as a solution.

SUMMARY
 Java API Documentation contains a frame injection vulnerability. 

VULNERABILITY DETAILS
VULNERABILITY DETAILS: 
CVEID: CVE-2013-1571

DESCRIPTION: HTML documentation generated by the Javadoc tool contains a security vulnerability. The vulnerability allows an attacker to craft a malicious link to the documentation which injects arbitrary content into the main frame. The injected content appears to originate from the site hosting the documentation, but in fact it is hosted elsewhere, and may contain malicious links or content. This type of attack is known as "clickjacking".

The attack does not require authentication and may be exploited remotely if the html page is network available, but some degree of specialized knowledge and techniques are required. An exploit would not impact the confidentiality of information or the availability of the system, but data integrity could be compromised.

title: IBM Cognos Territory and Quota Management 4.0.0 Enhancements - United States
text:
RELEASE NOTES

ABSTRACT
 This document outlines the new features and enhancements that were added to this release of IBM Cognos Territory and Quota Management. 

CONTENT
Activities | Assignments | Hierarchies | Reports 

Activities 

Support Case # Type Client Version Date Title [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27041406&aid=1] Enhancement 4.0.0 May 13, 2014 Multiple activity sets Description: Activities are now loaded into the Data tab. Users can create multiple data sets. This allows users with different sales transaction data with different structures to import multiple sets of data into the same instance of Cognos Territory and Quota Management.

Steps:  1. On the Data tab, click Add. 
 2. Type a name for the data set and, in the Type drop-down menu, select Crediting. 
 3. Click the data set link. 
 4. Click Load. 
 5. Click Browse to find your activities file. 
 6. Click Upload. 
 7. Tag each column.



Assignments Support Case # Type Client Version Date Title [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27041406&aid=1] Enhancement 4.0.0 May 13, 2014 Duplicate assignment sets Description: You can choose to make duplicates of assignment sets in Cognos Territory and Quota Management. This creates a sandbox environment that you can make changes to without affecting the current data. For example, you can create an exact duplicate of an assignment set, make changes to existing assignments, and propose new realignments.

When an assignment set is duplicated, the territories associated with the assignment set are also duplicated. You can select a date range for which to copy the rules and hierarchies. Any rule or node that is valid at some point in the specified date range is copied. Specifying a date range allows you to perform the following actions:
 * Exact copy - leave the start and end date blank. 
 * Copy active rules only - set the start and end date to today. 
 * Copy active and future rules - set the start date to today and leave the end date blank. 
 * Copy rules for next year - set the start date to January 1st of next year and the end date to Dec 31 of next year.


You can choose to copy the credit hierarchy, territory hierarchy, and overlay set mapped to the assignment set as well as an alternate data set. When the hierarchies and overly sets are copied you can choose to either keep the original hierarchy or create a copy of the hierarchy. When a copy of a hierarchy is created, only nodes that are active within the specified date range are copied into the new hierarchy. The duplicated assignment set is mapped to the new credit hierarchy and the duplicated territory set is mapped to the new territory hierarchy. When a copy of an overlay set is created, only rules from the set that are active within the specified date range are copied into the new overlay set. The duplicated overlay set is mapped to the new assignment set. You can select a different data set to use when the assignment set is copied, but the alternate data set must have the same structure as the original data set. That is the alternate data set must have the same attributes as the original data set. The new territory set is automatically mapped to the selected data set.

If you do not choose to copy the hierarchies, overlay set, or change the data set associated with the assignment set being copied, the following actions occur:
 * Assignment set rules that fit within the specified date range are copied. 
 * Territory rules that fit within the specified date range are copied. 
 * Credit hierarchy is not copied. The source Credit hierarchy is used in the new assignment set. 
 * Territory hierarchy is not copied. The source Territory hierarchy is used in the new territory set. 
 * Overlay set is not copied. If the source assignment set was mapped to an overlay set the same overlay set is mapped to the new assignment set. 
 * The same data set is used for the territory set.


Steps:  1.  On the Crediting tab, click Assignments. 
 2.  Select a folder. 
 3.  Click Create Sandbox. 
 4.  From the Assignments Sets drop-down menu, select the assignment set that you want to copy.
     The territories that are copied are determined by the assignment set selected. 
 5.  In the Sandbox Name field, type the suffix that you want to add to the end of the name of the copied assignment set. 
 6.  Select the date range for which to copy the rules and hierarchies.
     Any rule or node that is valid at some point during the specified date range is copied. 
 7.  To select hierarchies, overlay sets, and data sets to be copied, select the Advanced Options check box. 
 8.  To keep the original default hierarchy or overlay set associated with the duplicated assignment set, select Keep Original. 
 9.  To copy only nodes or rules in the hierarchy or overlay set that are active within the specified date range, select Create Copy.
     The duplicated assignment set or territory set is associated with the new hierarchy or overlay set. The new hierarchy or overlay set has the same name as the original with the suffix added. 
 10. To change the data set used by the territory set, select the new data set from the Data Set drop-down menu.
     The new data set must have the same attributes as the original. The new territory set is automatically mapped to the selected data set. 
 11. Click Copy.



Hierarchies Support Case # Type Client Version Date Title [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27041406&aid=1] Enhancement 4.0.0 May 13, 2014 Hierarchy nodes displayed in the format selected in the Display Options field Description: All node references on the Hierarchies page now honor the setting selected in the Display Options field. Parent and Alternate Hierarchy Parent nodes show both the name and description of the node when Show Both is selected in the Display Options field.

Steps:  1. On the Hierarchies page, select a hierarchy to view. 
 2. From the Display Options drop-down menu, select Show Both. 
 3. Select a node.

Support Case # Type Client Version Date Title [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27041406&aid=1] Enhancement 4.0.0 May 13, 2014 Date selection moved in toolbar Description: On the Hierarchies tab, the ability to select an effective date for which to view a hierarchy has been removed from the Date icon and placed in the Showing hierarchies for field. Users can now view hierarchies for a selected date by entering the date in the Showing hierarchies for field.

Steps:  1. On the Hierarchies page, in the Showing hierarchies for field, enter a date. 
 2. Press Enter.
    The hierarchies effective for the selected date are displayed.



Reports Support Case # Type Client Version Date Title [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27041406&aid=1] Enhancement 4.0.0 May 13, 2014 Assignment lookups Description: Users can now search for the territories and payees who are responsible for a transaction or account within given parameters. Users can look up the territory and sales people who are assigned to a sales territory by specific attributes, such as zip code or geographic location. This allows users to assign a new lead to the appropriate sales person. The assignment lookup search can be performed from within the application on the Reports page or through the CLI or Web Services.

NOTE: Overlays and overrides are not covered in the search. Assignment lookups are based on rules.

Steps:  1. In the Crediting module, select Reports. 
 2. In the Assignment Reports section, click Assignment Lookups. 
 3. Select an assignment set. 
 4. Type the values of the attributes for the territory and payee you want to look up. 
 5. Click Search.


Support Case # Type Client Version Date Title [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27041406&aid=1] Enhancement 4.0.0 May 13, 2014 Territory Ownership report Description: Users can now generate a report that displays the rules associated with a selected territory or assignee. 

Steps:  1. In the Crediting module, select Reports. 
 2. In the Territory Reports section, click Territory Ownership. 
 3. Select either the Territory Set or Assignment Set option. 
 4. Select a set from the Territory Set or Assignment Set drop-down menu.

 7. Click Apply.

title: IBM How to restore purged modules in IBM Rational DOORS using your backups - United States
text:
backup; DOORS; purge; delete; deleted; DB; database; server; production TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How do you restore purged modules using your backups in IBM Rational DOORS? 

CAUSE
The process on how to restore the purged module from the backups is not clear.

ANSWER
Once a module is purged, it is deleted permanently and can no longer be restored. This is outlined here [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21459624]. 

However, as the link above states, if you have backups of your DOORS data directory, you can restore the module from the backups. This is done by first restoring the entire DOORS database from your backup into a separate DOORS Database server and then copying the data of the purged module from the backup to an empty module created to replace the purged module.

Procedure:

1. Restore the backup of your DOORS database directory into a separate server
(e.g. the backup server) from your current production server.


2. Identify the .mod folder belonging to the purged module in the backup server data directory

3. Create a new empty module in your production server.


4. Identify the .mod folder belonging to the new empty module in the production server data directory


5. Stop both the DOORS production and backup servers.


6. Copy the contents of the purged module folder in the backup server to the empty module folder in the production server.


7. Restart the production server and check the empty module. It should now contain the purged module.



Detailed steps are below:

1. Create a separate backup DOORS database server using the process in the How to create additional IBM Rational DOORS database server services [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21656872] technote.


2. Restore the contents of your DOORS database data folder backup 
(e.g. DOORSHOME/data) into the data folder of the backup DOORS database created in 
Step 1 (in the technote above, this is the "newdoorsdata" folder).


3. When you connect the client to the temporary server, use the following steps to identify the
purged module ID in the backup server: 

 *  From the database explorer window, highlight the troubled module and Click Tools > Edit DXL
   
   Run the following DXL: print uniqueID getSelectedItem
   This will return output with the Unique IDs.
   
   Select the ID for the troubled module 
   For example: 00000080 My Module
   
   Search for mxxxxxxxx.mod folder in the current DOORS database
   (where xxxxxxxx is 00000080) 


4. In your production DOORS server, create an empty module in the same location as the 
purged module with the same module name and again use the steps from Step 3 to identify 
that module in your production DOORS database. 


5. Stop both the production and backup DOORS servers 


6. Copy the contents of the module directory you identified in Step 3 
into the directory you identified in Step 4. 


7. Restart the regular DOORS database server and log into DOORS. The contents of the 
module from the backup server should now be in your production server as it was in the 
last backup. 

Once this is complete, you can remove the shortcut to the backup DOORS server and delete its data directory. 


NOTE: A way to avoid having to restore the entire DOORS database is to make sure you identify a module .mod folder prior to purging it so that if you need to restore it, you will be able to go into the backups without needing to restore the entire database backup just to identify the purged module .mod folder. title: IBM EIF probe not receiving itm events - United States
text:
Title: IBM EIF probe not receiving itm events - United States

Text:
om_tec.conf eif probe itm event clearing omnibus TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 ITM is sending events to EIF probe which is then forwarded to the OMNIbus Server. Client is observing that the clearing event is sent per the ITM trace/log but the event does not seem to be received into EIF or OMNIbus as the triggered event is still seen in OMNIbus.



SYMPTOM
Situation in ITM is no longer true but event is not cleared in OMNIbus.


DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
The iptrace shows that the EIF probe on the OMNIbus side is resetting/closing(<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after it receives the event and it never shows up in the EIF logs, so the event is just dropped.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The solution is to set the connection_mode in your om_tec.config on the ITM Server (TEMS) to use 


connection_less 

instead of 

connection oriented.

That is, change this line in your om_tec.config

ConnectionMode=co
to
ConnectionMode=connection_less

You will need to restart the EIF on your ITM. (tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif)

Title: IBM How to enable Baselining in your monitored application. - United States

Text:
tema enable baselining Unknown application health status CAMADALL CAMADINST TECHNOTE (FAQ)

THIS DOCUMENT APPLIES ONLY TO THE FOLLOWING LANGUAGE VERSION(S):
 US English 

QUESTION
 Steps to enable Baselining in your monitored application. 

ANSWER
The health of the monitored application is calculated against an internally stored baseline threshold. The baselining of the application is a process that uses a pre-defined mathematical and statistical method to automatically calculate a threshold based on response time information typically collected over a period of time (few days to few weeks.) 

By default baselining gets enabled with a situation WasAppDiscoverd. This situation is enabled by default and will discover new applications then run a take action to start the baselining. So if this situation is not enabled then you should enable it and assign to the ITCAM App Server managing system list. 

You want to do baselining with normal or typical load on the server over a period of few days to few weeks, or even few months. The performance of the application under this load is considered good (you will see "Good"" in the Application Health views) and deviation from this performance indicates degrading health ("Bad" or "Fair" in the Application Health views) of the monitored application. 

To start baselining for your application server, please follow these steps: 

(Note 1: in this example, I've used a WebSphere-based application but you can also do the same for any application on your J2EE agent also.) 

(Note 2: Before beginning baselining, make sure you have typical or normal load on the server to set the baselining threshold values.) 

1. Login to your TEPS, select Application Health, right-click on it, go to Workspace and select Application Registry. Look at the panels on the right and observe the baselining columns. If they're blank, your baselining has not been started. 

2. Next select Application Health, right-click on it, go to Workspace and select Application Health status. If you see Unknown, then you know the baselining has not started or not been calculated. 

3. High-lite your application, select the small yellow chain link in the first unnamed column and select Application Configuration Details. See screenshot here: 

[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21653905&aid=1] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21653905&aid=1] 

4. In the bottom panel on the right select the line that says All and high-lite it. Then right-click it, select Take Action and Select. In the pull-down, select Start_Baselining and enter the Period (2 days), Update_Interval (every 2 hours), and Run_Clean set to 1 (clean start.) If you wish, you can change these values to whatever you want. 

See screenshots here:
[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21653905&aid=2] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21653905&aid=2]
[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21653905&aid=3]
Hit OK twice and you should get a Command completed successfully message. (Note: If you get a Baselining_Already_Active message in the pop-up window, then you should do another Take Action and Stop_Baselining first if you want to do the baselining again.)

Once you have the baselining active, let it run for the period of time with typical load on the server. After the baselining is complete, the Unknown values in the Application Health should now change to Good or Fair or Bad depending on threshold values.

title: IBM PI81386: SERIALIZATION PROBLEM BETWEEN DBFILQS0 AND DBFHEMH0. - United States
text:
z/os  A FIX IS AVAILABLE
Obtain the fix for this APAR.


SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  We are using Shared EMHQ and IETR for FP transactions..
   Just after IMS Cold Start, IMS CTL TCB entered infinite loop
   between DFSICIO0 and BRFTDD00 (IETR).
   This is because EMHB had EMHBIVI flag on for input processing,
   but CNT had CNTFF1I and CNTFF1SQ flags on for output processing.
   This is wrong combination.
   There was serialization problem between DBFILSQ0 and BRFTDDxx
   modules (IETR). At this time, IETR module was wrong. But same
   serialization problem exists between DBFILQS0 and DBFHEMH0 too,
   because DBFILQS0 runs under SQ2 TCB while DBFHEMH0 runs under
   CTL TCB. Both modules can update EMHB address on CTBFPTBA
   concurrently.
   There are next concerns.
   1. Compare Swap (CS) should be used when update CTBFPTBA.
   2. EMHBOVI flag need to be set before updating CTBFPTBA by
     DBFILQS0.
   3. DBFILQS0 is missing to obtain DBFEMHBL latch in share mode
     when updating CTBFPTBA.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:                                              *
   * IMSFP V14 Shared EMH users                                   *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:                                         *
   * Forward Fit of PI81349 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PI81349]:                                      *
   * Shared EMH Inform server does not serialize access when      *
   * updating EMHB pointer in CTBFPTBA.                           *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   * INSTALL CORRECTIVE SERVICE FOR APAR/PTF                      *
   ****************************************************************
   This loop problem was caused by IETR changing CTBFPTBA EMHB
   pointer regardless whether there was an EMHB with message
   pending.  IETR has been changed to not overlay CTBFPTBA when an
   EMHB has EMHBIVI or EMHBOVI set.
   -----
   DBFILQS0 does not serialize CTBFPTBA update when setting EMHB
   that it obtained for inform.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  GEN:
   KEYWORDS:
   
   *** END IMS KEYWORDS ***
   DBFEMHB and DBFILQS0 have been modified to address serialized
   access when updating CTBFPTBA:
   
   DBFEMHB:
   Add 4 EMHB trace entries: EMHBRTBB-EMHBRTBE
   
   DBFILQS0:
   Shared EMH Inform Queue Server, DBFILQS0, has been modified to
   preset EMHBIVI by DBFIQLS0 before attempting to queue
   the EMHB that it obtained for inform process.
   
   DBFILQS0 uses a compare-and-swap instruction to serialize
   CTBFPTBA to set the EMHB that it obtained for inform process.
   If another task has updated CTBFPTBA with another EMHB, then it
   would release the EMHB that it obtained and continue with

Informix; Performance; IC62006; TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Why do some SQL's seem to run slower prior to installing Informix Dynamic Server 11.50.xC6? 

CAUSE
You may be running into a known defect - APAR IC62006. 

This defect causes the optimizer to choose a much slower path than needed due to the incorrect calculation of the cost of the 'best' path. One way to test if this defect is impacting your queries performance is to use the 'ordered' clause as an optimizer directive "SELECT {+ explain ordered } ", this can be used as a workaround.

If you are already using 11.50.xC6 or greater and still experience slow running SQL's, you can use the following steps to help identify and narrow down the problem:
1 - Enable 'set explain;' within the query to get output of how the engine optimizes your query.
2 - Ensure update statistics has been run against all tables reference in the FROM clause, or in sub-queries.
3 - Remove one filter in the where clause to see if that makes a difference in performance of the query.
4 - Consider adding indexes to mimic join conditions within the filter.
5 - Consider using Optimizer directives to assist the optimizer in choosing the best plan/path for your query.



ANSWER
This has been identified as a product defect under APAR IC62006 fixed in 11.50.xC6 or greater

Title: IBM Switching Business Process Choreographer Explorer back to using HTTP from HTTPS - United States

Text:
 DOWNLOADABLE FILES

ABSTRACT
 In Business Process Manager Advanced Version 8.0.1, the default protocol used by Business Process Choreographer Explorer was changed to use HTTPS. You can switch it back to HTTP. 

DOWNLOAD DESCRIPTION
When Business Process Choreographer Explorer uses the default secure HTTPS protocol, any attempts to access Business Process Choreographer Explorer using HTTP are redirected to use HTTPS. If you need Business Process Choreographer Explorer to support insecure HTTP connections, you can use the unsecureExplorer.ant script to switch the protocol used from HTTPS to HTTP. 

Attention: It is not recommend to use the insecure HTTP protocol. Using HTTP for the Business Process Choreographer Explorer can open your organization to possible security problems.

Switching to HTTP

If you need to switch Business Process Choreographer Explorer from HTTPS to use HTTP, complete the following actions: 

 1. Download the unsecureExplorer.ant script file, which is attached near the bottom of this page.
    
    
 2. If you previously switched Business Process Choreographer Explorer to use HTTP, but are performing this task again because you are installing an interim fix, fix pack, or refresh pack that updated Business Process Choreographer Explorer has reverted it back to the default HTTPS protocol, you must first delete the old (invalid) backup EAR file before running the script.
    
     * On Linux, UNIX-based and z/OS platforms, delete the install_root/ProcessChoreographer/internal/bpcexplorer_secure_backup.ear file. 
     * On Microsoft Windows platforms, delete the
       install_root\ProcessChoreographer\internal\bpcexplorer_secure_backup.ear file.
       
       
    
    
 3. Run the script to patch the bpcexplorer.ear file. In a network deployment environment, you must run the script on the deployment manager.  * On Linux, UNIX-based and z/OS platforms, enter the following command:
       install_root/ws_ant.sh -f unsecureExplorer.ant 
     * On Windows platforms, enter the following command:
       install_root\ws_ant.bat -f unsecureExplorer.ant
       Note: A backup copy of the original EAR file is created named bpcexplorer_secure_backup.ear.
       
       
    
    
 4. Deploy the patched bpcexplorer.ear file by updating the profile. For more information about updating profiles for an interim fix, see one of the following documents:  * For version 8.0.1.x: Profile update instructions for IBM Business Process Manager (BPM) interim fixes [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21608414]. 
     * For version 8.5 and later: Profile update instructions for IBM Business Process Manager (BPM) interim fixes [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21637449].
       
       
    
    

Remember: In the future, if you install an interim fix, fix pack, or refresh pack that updates the Business Process Choreographer Explorer, it will revert to using the default secure HTTPS protocol. If that happens and you still need the Business Process Choreographer Explorer to use the HTTP protocol, you must complete these steps again to re-enable the HTTP protocol.
